content.title: About
content.content: Canned mango consists of ripe mango pieces packed in glass or metal jars with syrup or its own juice. The fruit retains its sweet, aromatic flavor and soft texture, while preserving most of its vitamins and minerals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mango is the national fruit of India and is often called the “king of fruits” in Asia.
Canning allows mango to be stored for several years without losing taste.
The syrup used is usually a simple sugar‑water solution, sometimes with added citric acid to stabilize colour.
Many brands offer “no added sugar” versions, making the product more diet‑friendly.
Canned mango is a popular ingredient in desserts, salads, and cocktails.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene, which converts to vitamin A, is beneficial for vision and skin.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in fluid balance and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Flavonoids and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet syrup can contain high levels of sugar, which is undesirable for people with diabetes or those watching their weight.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to mango.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain brands use preservatives (e.g., potassium sorbate) that can cause sensitivity.

items.title: Damaged cans
items.content: Do not consume from cans with dents or bulges, as they may indicate spoilage.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned mango can be eaten straight from the jar, added to yogurt, oatmeal, smoothies, salads, desserts, and baked goods. For a tangier taste, drain the syrup and replace it with lime juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, keep the jar refrigerated in its original container and consume within 5‑7 days.
